summary: This was a smoke-test task (verify GLM-5.2 proxy routing) whose only intended output per the worker's own PROGRESS.md was a one-line HTML comment appended to README.md. The checkpoint commit instead swept in two massive generated Drizzle artifacts — drizzle/0001_wakeful_reptil.sql (6,080 lines: a full-schema dump of 434 CREATE TABLE statements and hundreds of ENUMs, including ALTER TYPE ADD VALUE for user_role/notification_type) and drizzle/meta/0001_snapshot.json (37,005 lines). These are not smoke-test output; they were produced by `bun run db:generate` (a fresh snapshot/migration emitted from schema.ts) and accidentally committed. The generated migration number collides with an existing migration on main: `0001_wakeful_reptil.sql` reuses number 0001 already taken by `drizzle/0001_mcp_access_codes.sql` (committed at 33b615ba). I confirmed this directly: `node scripts/check-migration-collision.mjs` fails with 'ERROR: New migration file reuses a number that already exists on main! Number 0001: Existing 0001_mcp_access_codes.sql, New 0001_wakeful_reptil.sql'. Applying this migration to any database would attempt to recreate the entire compliance/platform schema (CREATE SCHEMA, hundreds of CREATE TYPE, 434 CREATE TABLE) that already exists, failing on the very first statement (`CREATE SCHEMA "platform"`/`CREATE SCHEMA "compliance"`) — it is un-runnable and the collision check the repo ships would block CI. The worker's PROGRESS.md claims it 'EXECUTED every CI gate from ci.yml' and that all passed including 'Doc Cross-References (341/341)', but it did not run the migration-collision check that is part of the repo's guardrail suite (PROGRESS explicitly lists only guardrail-presence, asset-registry, metadata-index, doc-quarantine, doc-cross-references — not check-migration-collision), so the claim of 'all pass' is misleading. The legitimate content of this task is solely the README.md one-liner and the PROGRESS.md status rewrite; the drizzle/ files and the _journal.json edit must be removed before this can be considered for merge. No .github/workflows/** files are touched, so the hard workflow-scope rule is not implicated. Recommend reject and a follow-up to drop drizzle/0001_wakeful_reptil.sql, drizzle/meta/0001_snapshot.json, and the _journal.json entry, then re-verify against check-migration-collision.mjs.
issues: Generated Drizzle migration + snapshot (drizzle/0001_wakeful_reptil.sql, drizzle/meta/0001_snapshot.json, drizzle/meta/_journal.json) committed as part of a smoke-test that should have produced no schema artifacts — these must be dropped.

Migration-number collision: 0001_wakeful_reptil reuses number 0001 already taken on main by 0001_mcp_access_codes.sql; scripts/check-migration-collision.mjs fails. Would block CI and is un-runnable (tries to CREATE SCHEMA/CREATE TABLE for the entire existing schema).

Migration content is a full-schema dump (434 CREATE TABLE, ALTER TYPE ADD VALUE on user_role/notification_type) — applying it on any existing DB fails immediately on CREATE SCHEMA "platform" and would corrupt/number-collide the migration journal.
PROGRESS.md's 'all CI gates pass' claim omits check-migration-collision.mjs (the one gate this change actually trips), so the self-reported verification is incomplete/misleading.
drizzle/meta/_journal.json lost its trailing newline (now ends without a newline) — minor but a formatting regression in a tracked file.
